title: Adaptive Onboarding Orchestration for Mixed-Precision and Prompt Sensitivity
author: Maya Thompson
summary: A cross-functional orchestration guide for onboarding models whose behavior is sensitive to prompt families and mixed-precision quantization. Defines stages, telemetry signals, automated hedging mechanisms, and an integrated regression triage path to reduce surprises during promotion to Dedicated and Private deployments.
content:
Overview

This document defines the Adaptive Onboarding Orchestration (AAO) used to certify models for production serving where two operational dimensions interact strongly: (1) prompt-pair / prompt-family sensitivity and (2) mixed-precision / quantization variants. The AAO coordinates eval-harness runs, probe synthesis, shadow fleets, quantized artifact validation, and a regression triage escalation path so we can safely migrate models across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes with predictable token-quality economics.

Goals
- Reduce first-24-hour regression incidents after model promotion by 80% compared to ad-hoc onboarding.
- Surface prompt-family failures and quant-compatibility failures with deterministic triage artifacts.
- Automate hedging: the runtime can route requests to a fallback precision/model variant using an ownership policy and telemetry guardrail.

Scope and applicability
- Applies to models being onboarded to the Redwood serving runtime where:
  - A quantized artifact (fp16, int8, mixed) will be produced, or
  - The model is known to have prompt sensitivity across core customer slices (e.g., conversational templates, financial instruction patterns, legal Q&A), or
  - The model will be promoted into Dedicated or Private plans where rollback or fallout is costly.
- Not intended for small experimental snapshots (< 10k synthetic probes) or research-only forks.

Key concepts and definitions
- Prompt sensitivity map (PSM): A structured mapping of prompt families (canonical templates + perturbations) to expected behavioral contracts (e.g., factuality, refusal-rate, formatting).
- Precision hedging: Runtime routing rules that prefer a cheaper quantized variant but automatically route to a higher-precision fallback when quality signals cross thresholds.
- Probe fabric: A synthesized and live-sourced set of evaluation probes derived from customer telemetry, historical slices, and synthetics for coverage.
- Hedging policy: A JSON/YAML spec that enumerates signals, thresholds, and fallback targets used by the Smart Router.

Owners and stakeholders
- Primary owner: Applied ML Onboarding (engineering)
- Service owners: Runtime Scheduling, Telemetry, Eval-Harness
- Reviewers: Model Safety, QA, Product (appropriate product owner per model)

Success criteria (promotion gate)
1. Coverage: PSM includes >= 30 canonical families, each with >= 50 probe variants (synthetic + seeded live).
2. Quant parity: For target quant profile (e.g., int8-mixed), fidelity delta <= 2.5% on coherence and factuality slices; any larger deltas have documented mitigation strategies.
3. Production-like shadow: 24-hour shadow run with at least 10M tokens and no more than 1 Sev-2 regressions attributable to model behavior.
4. Triaging latency: Root-cause hypothesis created within 2 business hours for any sentinel failure during shadow (see regression triage path).

AAO stages (high level)
1) Preflight: PSM authoring, probe fabric assembly, quant-profile candidate generation
2) Simulated evals: Eval-harness runs across mixed seed sets, generate fidelity matrices and delta heatmaps
3) Shadow mesh: Canary shadow across heterogeneous workload replicas (small percent of traffic) with hedging enabled
4) Live validation: Nightly production-mirroring sweeps for 72 hours and human-in-the-loop review for flagged slices
5) Promotion and burn-in: Timed rollout (0 -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with telemetry gating and automated rollback policies

Detailed procedures
A. Preflight checklist (step-by-step)
1. Create Prompt Sensitivity Map (PSM) document tied to model: include canonical prompts, perturbation strategies, and a definition of expected output contracts.
2. Query telemetry: pull top-10k most-common templates for the service(s) the model will serve. Redact PII.
3. Synthesize probes: for each PSM family generate: 50 synthetic variants, 30 adversarial/paraphrase variants, and 20 long-context variants.
4. Define quant candidate list: baseline fp16, target int8-mixed candidate, and optional per-layer mixed precision plan.
5. Register artifact in eval-harness with meta: model_id, quant_profile_id, psmap_id, owner, expected_latency SLOs.

B. Simulated evals (automation)
- Run the eval-harness with the following job matrix:
  - Seeds: deterministic seed set (seed-anchored), 10 stochastic seeds, and long-tail probe sample.
  - Metrics: Coherence (P1), Factuality (P2), Refusal/Policy violations (P3), Formatting fidelity (P4), Latency percentiles (P5).
  - Output: heatmap artifacts (CSV), delta-summaries (JSON) and counterfactual examples (annotated).
- Pass criteria: no PSM family has a P1 or P2 regression > 3% compared to baseline; any failures create a triage ticket.

C. Shadow mesh orchestration
1. Provision shadow slices in Dedicated/Dedicated-like environment.
2. Attach hedging policy: example YAML spec below.

Hedging policy example YAML:
---
policy_name: "int8-hedge-alpha"
owner: "applied-ml-onboarding"
signals:
  - name: "coherence_delta"
    type: "percent_delta"
    window: "5m"
    threshold: 3.0
  - name: "factuality_drop"
    type: "absolute_drop"
    window: "1h"
    threshold: 2.0
fallbacks:
  - condition: "coherence_delta > 3.0 or factuality_drop > 2.0"
    target: "fp16-stable-v1"
    cooldown: "10m"
---

3. Runtime wiring: the Smart Router will evaluate incoming request against the latest hedging policy and runtime signal stream; if any condition matches, the request is routed to the fallback target and an event is emitted to the triage DAG.

D. Live validation and human review
- Assign annotators to flagged counterfactuals with SLA: annotate within 8 hours for Severity >= 2, 24 hours for Severity 3.
- Use the evaluation dashboard to filter by PSM family and quant_profile.
- If annotator consensus indicates a regression, invoke the Regression Triage Path.

Regression triage path (short)
1. Triage ticket auto-created with: failing probe IDs, seed, quant_profile, eval-harness logs, and a sample of live traces.
2. On-call applied-ml engineer owns initial hypothesis within 2 hours and assigns to a specialist if needed.
3. Run differential artifacts: (a) replay failing probes against baseline and candidate artifacts, (b) per-layer attention/activation snapshots if available.
4. Classification: classify cause as one of: tokenization mismatch, quantization artifact, prompt engineering mismatch, data drift, or runtime bug.
5. Remediation: either (a) create a prompt rewrite patch, (b) tighten hedging thresholds, (c) revert to higher-precision artifact, or (d) deploy a targeted rollback to impacted tenant cohorts.
6. Postmortem: a short RCA and corrective action are posted to the related pages in the onboarding registry within 5 business days.

Telemetry & signals (what to monitor)
- Fidelity signals: per-slice coherence_delta, factuality_drop, refusal_rate_delta, hallucination_index (annotator-derived heuristic).
- Infrastructure signals: tail latency p99, request queue length growth, kv-cache-hit-rate by shard.
- Economic signals: average token cost delta, requests-per-second vs. expected throughput.
- Triaged artifacts: number of active triage tickets, mean time to hypothesis, and remediation classification distribution.

Templates and example queries
- Eval-harness job CLI example:
  rwi-eval run --model model-v3 --probes psmap:finance-kw --quant int8-mixed --out /tmp/eval_artifact --seeds 0,1,2,3 --metrics coherence,factuality,latency

- Probe manifest (CSV header example):
  probe_id,psm_family,variant_type,seed,context_length,expected_contract_tag
  p-000123,account-summary,synthetic,42,256,factuality:high

- Minimal rollout hedging config (JSON):
  {
    "policy_name": "min-hedge-2026",
    "signals": [
      {"name": "coherence_delta", "threshold": 4.0, "window": "10m"},
      {"name": "refusal_rate_delta", "threshold": 5.0, "window": "1h"}
    ],
    "fallback": "fp16-stable-v1",
    "notify_channels": ["#onboarding-alerts", "pager:duty-oncall"]
  }

Escalation matrix and SLAs
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev-1: Customer-facing data-safety or legal violation — page and escalate immediately.
  - Sev-2: Major fidelity regression causing incorrect outputs in a core slice — oncall within 1 hour.
  - Sev-3: Minor formatting/regression that affects UX but has a workaround — respond within 8 hours.
- SLA: initial hypothesis or reassign within 2 hours for Sev-2 and Sev-1; mitigation or rollback decision within 4 hours.

When to stop and roll back
- Hard rollback triggers (automated):
  - Any PSM family with factuality_drop > 5% in a production shadow window.
  - Hallucination index spike above configured threshold for 30 minutes.
  - Active Sev-1 incident tied to model artifact.

Best practices and anti-patterns
- Best: keep probe fabric curated; include adversarial paraphrases; run multi-seed simulations before any shadow traffic.
- Anti-pattern: relying solely on microbench fideltas (token-level) without human-anchored semantics checks.

Related pages
- Link the model registry entry, PSM authoring template, and hedging policy schema. (Use the onboarding registry to find the IDs.)

Appendix A: Example postmortem summary template
- Title: [ModelID] [QuantProfile] Regression summary
- Window: timestamp range
- Impacted PSM families: list
- Severity: classification
- Evidence: top 10 failing probes + annotated consensus
- Root cause hypothesis: short statement
- Action taken: hedging tightened / rollback / prompt patch / quant retune
- Owners: persons and teams
- Follow-ups: scheduled tasks with due dates

Appendix B: Quick reference cheat-sheet
- Required artifacts to register: PSM ID, probe_manifest.csv, quant_profile.json, hedging_policy.yaml, eval_artifact.zip
- Minimum probe sizes per family: 100 (production-grade), 30 (small-surface), 10 (experimental)
- Contact: #onboarding Slack channel and oncall pager
